Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres, slightly soft
hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows where one
sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph / stencil print
grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Details are built from small cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
wood planks), not painted lines.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha, no chroma-key colour
behind it, no coloured fringe), every object complete and separated by clear transparent
gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the object, no text, no captions, no logos.
View: front-facing, very slight three-quarter, the same for every object on the sheet.

Generate ONLY the actual Tainan Panggong stone arch, a three-quarter view with near end at lower LEFT and distant end at upper RIGHT. Image 1 is the approved frontal cutout and the geometric model. Image 2 is the approved building and the flat fibrous cut-paper material and printed grain reference. Images 3–5 are photos to consult for the real geometry, proportions, and lions. Exactly four tall square stone pillars in one row, exactly three unobstructed open bays with true alpha; center opening notably wider and higher, both lateral openings narrower. The structure recedes diagonally upwards to the right with slim visible side faces and visible differences in scale from near left to far right. Straight stacked stone lintels, with a very small plain stepped stone top over the center. Straight squared beam ends like the approved artwork, no upturned eaves, curling ridge ornament, gourd or running horses. Low-relief subdued paper shapes only. Small guardian stone lions on the front and rear of each pillar foot, with rear lions visible where the viewpoint allows. Omit inscriptions. Grey beige muted warm stone with visible paper fibres, cut edges and risograph grain; a handful of very thin flat paper layers, no 3D stone modelling. No external shadow, halo, pavement, buildings or other objects. Complete isolated arch with transparent margin.

Perspective correction takes priority: use a shallow orthographic three-quarter projection, so both the feet and the beams rise diagonally to the right. Imagine the pillar baselines at image coordinates (15%,90%), (32%,84%), (64%,72%), (82%,65%). The straight top edges of the connecting beams follow the SAME upward-to-right axis as the feet, never sloping down to the right. Draw equal vertical post lengths in this orthographic projection. Lions are small, simplified shallow paper cutouts with only two or three stacked tonal layers, consistent with the reference museum's flat paper trim. Minimize pillar thickness and contact shadows. Grey-beige rather than yellow-beige. Keep all contours clean and open to the native alpha.
